newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela oil price rises as OPEC signals calm.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oil price rises as OPEC signals calm.

text.p: Venezuela's basket price of crude oil and oil products rose 40 cents per barrel to end the week at $16.45 per barrel, according to a Ministry of Energy and Mines statement issued on Friday.
Oil traders in London attributed the firmer tone to supportive comments by OPEC ministers meeting in Iran, but it hardly dented a 20 percent slump in prices earlier this year.
Seven OPEC ministers met in the Persian city of Isfahan on Thursday and renewed pledges to stick to individual crude production quotas under OPEC's long-ignored ceiling.
But analysts said they saw no chance of OPEC's biggest quota busters, heavily represented in Isfahan by Venezuela and Nigeria, standing by their renewed promise.
"I simply don't believe it," veteran OPEC watcher Mehdi Varzi of Kleinwort Benson told Reuters in Isfahan. "I would be amazed if the likes of Venezuela reined back output."

Venezuela's basket price ended 1996 with one of the highest averages for several years at $18.39 per barrel. But since then, the basket has slid to average $16.75 in March and $15.69 last month, according to adjusted Ministry figures.
So far this year, the basket has averaged $17.66 per barrel, down from $17.88 last week, the Ministry said.

Venezuela's government has based its 1997 budget on an average price for the year of $14.00 per barrel, although Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta has said he expects it to average higher than $15.50.
